chunks: And from him, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wael, from Hudhaifah, that he said:

I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when the Mahdi was mentioned in his presence say: 'Indeed, allegiance will be given to him between the Rukn and the Maqam. His name is Ahmad, Abdullah, and al-Mahdi; these are his three names.'

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ: Ahmad, one of the names of the Mahdi
key_terms.الرُّكْنُ: The Rukn, a specific corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمَقَامُ: The Maqam, the station of Abraham near the Kaaba
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيّ: The Guided One, a title for the twelfth Imam
key_terms.عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: Abdullah, one of the names of the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What are the three names of Imam Mahdi mentioned in this hadith and where will his allegiance be given?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological sign of the Mahdi’s public allegiance (bay'ah) at the sacred site of the Kaaba, specifically between the Rukn and Maqam. It underscores the Shia belief in the Mahdi’s multiple names, including Ahmad and Abdullah, linking him to the Prophet’s lineage and prophetic tradition. The narration serves as a key indicator for believers during the period of Major Occultation, affirming the legitimacy of his eventual reappearance.
